userStories.title: Serialize session settings and refuse a deleted session under the resume lock
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Serialize settings mutations per session and re-check stored-session existence under the resume lock so settings updates cannot undo a permission downgrade and resumes cannot resurrect deleted sessions.

**Motivation** — The probe observed `full → read → full`, with both requests succeeding.

**Approach** — Implement the following Target design, not the baseline.

`setMode` / `setConfigOption` in `createSessionRegistry` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/registry.ts`):
The registry keeps a private `Map<string, Promise<void>>` of settings tails keyed by session id. A new private helper `serializeSettings<T>(sessionId, work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` invokes `work` synchronously, in the same tick, when no tail is stored for the session (so an uncontended call runs up to its first await exactly as today); otherwise it chains `work` after the stored tail (ignoring the tail's rejection). It stores the muted new tail and deletes the map entry in a `finally` when it is still the stored tail. `setMode` and `setConfigOption` run their whole body inside it: `entryOf(sessionId)`, the `apply*Change(settingsOf(entry.meta), ...)` computation, `applySettings`, and (for `setConfigOption`) the returned `configOptions(next, options.tiers)`. So the second of two overlapping calls computes from the metadata the first one persisted. A rejected mutation does not block the next one. Behaviour change: at baseline the second of two overlapping calls on one session is refused with `turnInProgress()` once the first has entered `ServerSession.switchTo`; it now waits and runs. No existing test pins the refusal. Prompts are not serialized: a turn started during a held credential lookup still runs and still records its metadata, as today.

`openEntry` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/registry.ts`) and `openStored` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/registry-open.ts`):
`openEntry` gains a fourth parameter `opts?: { readonly requireStored?: boolean }`. When `requireStored` is true, right after `acquireLock` resolves and inside the existing `try`, it calls `deps.storage.readMeta(meta.sessionId)`; only existence is checked (the open proceeds with the metadata `openStored` read). A `null` result throws `unknownSession(meta.sessionId)`, so the existing `catch` releases the lock before rethrowing (MCP has not been started yet). `openStored` passes `{ requireStored: true }` through `openAndReplay`; `create` does not. The `createReopen` deps type gains the parameter.

Failure handling: The first of two queued settings mutations rejects — The second still runs, computing from the metadata as it then stands. Only the first caller sees the error. A resume finds its metadata gone after taking the lock — It rejects with `unknownSession(sessionId)`, releases the lock, opens no session and writes no metadata.

Fixture for the ACs that name the overlap fixture: The "overlap fixture" below is: a registry from `setupRegistry` whose `ensureCredentials` resolves at once on its first call (the `create` open) and is held pending on its second call. A session is created and switched to mode `full` with `registry.setMode`. `registry.setConfigOption(sessionId, "model", "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5")` is then started and parks on the held lookup, and `registry.setMode(sessionId, "read")` is started while it is parked.

**Scope** — In: registry settings serialization, under-lock existence re-check for stored opens, ReopenDeps argument propagation, and deterministic integration regressions in the new registry-settings-queue.test.ts using existing setupRegistry seams. Out: pre-dispatch turn cancellation (US-002) and instruction-delivery persistence (US-003). US-001 only: prompts are not serialized with settings mutations; a turn that starts while a settings mutation is queued is refused or allowed by the existing `entry.server.running` check, as today. US-001 only: the settings queue is per registry instance; mutations of one session from separate server processes are not coordinated. US-001 only: a `delete` that races an in-flight `openStored` before the open takes its lock is answered by the re-check under the lock; `delete` does not wait for or cancel the in-flight open. US-001 only: a close or delete of the session while a settings mutation is queued is not coordinated with the queue; the queued mutation rejects with `unknownSession` from `entryOf`. US-001 only: the resume re-check under the lock verifies only that the metadata still exists; a mode or model changed by another process between the pre-lock read and the lock is not picked up.

**Interface** — `serializeSettings<T>(sessionId, work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>`; `opts?: { readonly requireStored?: boolean }` is the fourth `openEntry` parameter; `openStored` passes `{ requireStored: true }` through `openAndReplay`. Public registry method signatures remain unchanged.

**Testing** — Use three-session-tdd: isolated failing regression tests against the baseline first, then implementation without test edits, then verification. Controls explicitly marked below already pass on baseline. Reuse the held-credentials and priced(costUsd) patterns from registry-races.test.ts and failOpens/release accounting from setupRegistry. Keep gates deterministic, release them in cleanup, and do not start real adapters.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] In the overlap fixture, when the held credential lookup is released, Promise.all of registry.setConfigOption and registry.setMode resolves successfully.
[integration] In the overlap fixture, after both mutations resolve, storage.readMeta(sessionId) returns settings matching { mode: 'read', model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5' }.
[integration] In the overlap fixture, after release and settlement, the last openSession request in opened matches { profile: 'read', model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5' }.
[integration] In the overlap fixture, while the credential lookup is held, starting registry.setMode(sessionId, 'read') adds no request to opened.
[integration] In the overlap fixture, after release, opened records the model-switch request before the mode-switch request.

[integration; control] In the overlap fixture, registry.get(sessionId).prompt with the priced(0.25) script completes while the credential lookup is still held, before release, and after both settings calls resolve storage.readMeta(sessionId).costUsd is 0.25.

[integration; control] When registry.setConfigOption to 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5' is awaited before registry.setMode(sessionId, 'read') on a created session, storage.readMeta(sessionId) returns settings matching { mode: 'read', model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5' }.

[integration] Given setupRegistry with failOpens: [2] (create is open 1, the failing switch is open 2, its restore is open 3), when registry.setMode(sessionId, 'full') and registry.setMode(sessionId, 'read') start in the same tick on a created session, their settlement statuses are respectively rejected and fulfilled (only the first caller sees the failure), and storage.readMeta(sessionId).mode is 'read'.

[integration; control] An uncontended registry.setConfigOption(sessionId, 'model', 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5') on a created session calls ensureCredentials for the new model in the same tick it is called, before any await.

[integration] Given a session created and closed with registry.close, when registry.resume(sessionId, input) is started with ensureCredentials held on call 2 (create was call 1), a signal that the held call was entered is awaited (so readMeta has resolved) before registry.delete(sessionId) is called and resolves, and the lookup is then released, registry.resume rejects with the same error code as registry.resume of a never-created id.

[integration] In the resume-versus-delete case (a session created and closed with registry.close; registry.resume(sessionId, input) started with ensureCredentials held on call 2 (create was call 1) and the held call's entry awaited so readMeta has resolved; registry.delete(sessionId) called and resolved; the lookup then released), openSession is not called for registry.resume.

[integration] In the resume-versus-delete case (a session created and closed with registry.close; registry.resume(sessionId, input) started with ensureCredentials held on call 2 (create was call 1) and the held call's entry awaited so readMeta has resolved; registry.delete(sessionId) called and resolved; the lookup then released), after registry.resume settles, releases() equals 3: close, delete and resume's own lock.

[integration; control] In the resume-versus-delete case (a session created and closed with registry.close; registry.resume(sessionId, input) started with ensureCredentials held on call 2 (create was call 1) and the held call's entry awaited so readMeta has resolved; registry.delete(sessionId) called and resolved; the lookup then released), storage.hasMeta(sessionId) is false after registry.resume settles, with no metadata recreated by the refused resume.
[integration; control] When registry.resume reopens a closed session that was not deleted, its resolved session state reports the stored mode and model.

[integration; control] When registry.delete removes a closed session with no resume in flight, storage.hasMeta(sessionId) is false, and a later registry.resume of that id rejects with the not-found error code.

routing.reasoning: Two existing production modules need a private promise-tail queue patterned on createReopen and an existence check inside existing lock cleanup; the changes are bounded, but credential ordering and permission-mode/session safety require the three-session-tdd security override.

userStories.title: Suppress prompt dispatch for a turn cancelled before dispatch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — End a pre-dispatch-cancelled turn without sending a prompt or cancel notification to the agent.

**Motivation** — A cancel during those awaits reaches the agent as `session/prompt` followed by `session/cancel`.

**Approach** — Implement the following Target design for `promptOnce` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/turn.ts`):
Before calling `state.link.prompt`, when `input.signal.aborted` is true, it builds `reason = abortReason(input.signal)`, attaches `unansweredSpend(carried)` with `attachTurnSpend`, and throws `reason`; no `session/prompt` and no `session/cancel` is sent. `runPromptTurn`'s denial-continuation check is unchanged (it already reads `!input.signal.aborted` with no await before the next dispatch).

Failure handling: The turn signal is aborted before the first dispatch — No `session/prompt` is sent; the turn ends `cancelled` with zero tokens. Preserve carried spend if present using the existing unansweredSpend helper, not a newly invented accounting rule. Keep abortReason, NO_RESPONSE_SPEND, unansweredSpend, cancelTurn and the facade's fromError mapping as existing integration points; no change to the nax-agent turn runner is required.

The "held-marker fixture" below is: a session opened through `createAgentSession` over `acpBackend` and an `inMemoryAgent`, with a transcript store wrapping `createMemoryTranscriptStore` whose `markTurn` for the state `running` waits on a held promise. `AgentSession.send("look")` is iterated; on its `turn_start` event `AgentSession.cancel()` is called, and then the held `markTurn` is released.

**Scope** — In: promptOnce's pre-dispatch guard and facade-driven regressions in turn-cancel-before-dispatch.test.ts. Out: settings serialization and resume/delete locking (US-001), and instruction-delivery persistence (US-003). US-002 only: an abort that arrives after the first `session/prompt` was sent keeps today's `session/cancel` plus grace behaviour. US-002 only: `liveFor` may still reconnect a crashed agent process for an already-aborted turn; only the prompt dispatch is guarded.

**Interface** — The spec retains the existing `promptOnce`, `runPromptTurn`, `abortReason(signal)`, `unansweredSpend(carried)` and `cancelTurn` interfaces; `attachTurnSpend` is imported from `@nathapp/nax-agent`. There is no public signature change.

**Testing** — Use three-session-tdd with tests against baseline before source edits. Exercise createAgentSession, AgentSession.send/cancel, the held running marker and inMemoryAgent.callsTo through the sanctioned launch seam. Script 7 input and 3 output tokens to prove that pre-dispatch cancellation never reaches the scripted response; retain the post-dispatch one-prompt/one-cancel grace control and a successful second send on the same session. Restore seams and release held promises in cleanup; use no real adapters.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] In the held-marker fixture, after cancellation and marker release, inMemoryAgent.callsTo('session/prompt') is empty.
[integration] In the held-marker fixture, after cancellation and marker release, inMemoryAgent.callsTo('session/cancel') is empty.
[integration; control] In the held-marker fixture, the terminal turn_end event of AgentSession.send has status 'cancelled'.

[integration] In the held-marker fixture with inMemoryAgent scripted to answer a prompt with 7 input and 3 output tokens, the terminal turn_end event reports usage matching { inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0 }.

[integration; control] When AgentSession.cancel() is called after inMemoryAgent has received the session/prompt and it answers 'cancelled' within the grace, inMemoryAgent received exactly one session/prompt and one session/cancel, and the terminal turn_end status is 'cancelled'.

[integration; control] After the held-marker fixture's cancelled turn, a second AgentSession.send('again') on the same session adds exactly one session/prompt to inMemoryAgent.callsTo('session/prompt') and ends with status 'completed'.

routing.reasoning: A single-file pre-dispatch guard reuses abortReason, unansweredSpend and attachTurnSpend with no new production abstraction; session cancellation still requires the three-session-tdd security override, with facade-level tests proving wire and accounting behavior.

userStories.title: Persist actual ACP instruction delivery across explicit resume
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist whether session instructions reached the agent and prefer that record on explicit resume while preserving legacy transcript behavior.

**Motivation** — A first turn rejected locally (`ACP_IMAGE_INPUT_UNSUPPORTED`, thrown in `sendTurn` after the turn marker is written) sends zero prompts, yet the marker exists, so after close and explicit resume the first text prompt omits the instructions.

**Approach** — Implement the following Target designs, not the baseline.

`TranscriptAcpRecord` (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-types.ts`):
Gains `readonly instructionsDelivered?: boolean` — whether the agent has received the session instructions. Absent means "not recorded" (a document written before this feature).

`initialDoc` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts`):
When the session is opened with non-empty `instructions`, the new document's `acp` record carries `instructionsDelivered: false`. A session opened without non-empty instructions (undefined or `""`) writes no `instructionsDelivered` field, and `saveDelivery` runs only when `ctx.instructions` is non-empty, so a later resume that supplies instructions keeps today's turn-marker rule.

`Restore` and `storedSessionOf` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/resume.ts`):
`Restore` gains `readonly instructionsDelivered?: boolean`, set from `doc.acp.instructionsDelivered` only when it is a boolean; any other value is treated as absent.

`openBackend`, `AcpSession` and `sendTurn` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/backend.ts`):
`instructionsSent: restore?.instructionsDelivered ?? ctx.resume?.doc.turn !== undefined` — a recorded value wins, and a document without the field keeps the turn-marker rule (user ruling 2026-11-24: legacy documents are assumed delivered). `AcpSession` gains `deliverySaved: boolean`, initially `instructionsSent`. In `sendTurn`'s `finally`, after `saveBaseline`, when `s.ctx.instructions` is non-empty and `s.instructionsSent && !s.deliverySaved`, a new `saveDelivery(s)` load-merges `acp: { ...doc.acp, instructionsDelivered: true }` into the stored document (skipping a document with no `acp` record, as `saveBaseline` does) and sets `deliverySaved`. Like `saveBaseline` it is best effort: a failure is logged with `warn("Could not save the ACP instruction delivery", sessionId)` and never fails the turn.

Failure handling: Saving the delivery record fails — `Could not save the ACP instruction delivery` is logged at warn; the turn's result is unchanged; the stored value stays `false`; the next completed turn tries again. A stored `instructionsDelivered` is not a boolean — Treated as absent: the turn-marker rule decides. Do not change the existing #2364 receipt callback semantics: instructionsSent becomes true on real receipt, not merely a turn marker or attempted dispatch.

The "delivery fixture" below is: a session opened through `createAgentSession` over `acpBackend` and an `inMemoryAgent` that advertises `session/resume` (the `RESUMABLE` capabilities of `backend-resume.test.ts`) and whose prompt capabilities exclude images, with `instructions` `RULES` and one `createMemoryTranscriptStore` shared by the open and any later `resumeAgentSession`.

**Scope** — In: documented optional TranscriptAcpRecord field in nax-agent (type-only, no runtime change), initial ACP document field, boolean-only restore extraction, backend delivery state and best-effort load-merge persistence, and facade-level regressions in backend-instruction-delivery.test.ts. The binding workdir remains packages/nax-agent-acp, with the specified type-only file change in packages/nax-agent. Out: server settings/resume-lock races (US-001) and pre-dispatch cancellation guard (US-002). Existing transcript documents are not migrated; a document without `instructionsDelivered` keeps the turn-marker rule. US-003 only: a reconnect after an agent crash keeps the in-memory `instructionsSent` flag and does not re-read the delivery record. Revising the design rule in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-acp-fix-bundle-2364-2366-2367-design.md` (section 4, "Initial value is unchanged") to describe the persisted delivery record is a manual edit made with this spec; no story edits it.

**Interface** — `readonly instructionsDelivered?: boolean` on both `TranscriptAcpRecord` and `Restore`; `deliverySaved: boolean` on `AcpSession`; `instructionsSent: restore?.instructionsDelivered ?? ctx.resume?.doc.turn !== undefined`; new `saveDelivery(s)` following saveBaseline's best-effort load-merge pattern.

**Testing** — Use three-session-tdd with baseline regressions before source changes and unchanged tests during implementation. Reuse the shared-store explicit-resume harness and RESUMABLE capabilities of backend-resume.test.ts and the unsupported-image fixture from backend-images.test.ts, using only inMemoryAgent and _acpBackendDeps.launch. Verify false/true persistence, exact prompt text after resume, legacy/no-marker behavior, explicit false precedence, non-boolean fallback, omitted/empty instructions, and a store that throws only once for the true-delivery write. Capture warnings through setAgentLogger from @nathapp/nax-agent and restore logger/launch seams and sessions in cleanup. Ensure baseline and delivery writes merge the latest document rather than discarding turn markers, identity or cost.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] In the delivery fixture, immediately after createAgentSession resolves, the stored document's acp.instructionsDelivered is false.

[integration] In the delivery fixture, a first AgentSession.send('look', { images: [img] }) ends with turn_end matching { status: 'errored', error: { code: 'ACP_IMAGE_INPUT_UNSUPPORTED' } }, and afterwards the stored acp.instructionsDelivered is still false.

[integration] In the delivery fixture, after the rejected image turn, close() and resumeAgentSession with the same store and instructions 'RULES', the first AgentSession.send('next') reaches inMemoryAgent as a session/prompt whose text block is 'RULES\n\nnext'.
[integration] In the delivery fixture, after a first text AgentSession.send that inMemoryAgent answers with message content, the stored acp.instructionsDelivered is true.

[integration; control] In the delivery fixture, after a first text AgentSession.send that inMemoryAgent answers with message content, close() and resumeAgentSession with the same store and instructions 'RULES', the next AgentSession.send('next') reaches inMemoryAgent with text block 'next'.

[integration; control] Given a stored document with a valid acp record (agentSessionId, agent, cwd), no instructionsDelivered field and a turn marker, when resumeAgentSession restores it with instructions 'RULES', the next AgentSession.send('next') sends text block 'next'.

[integration; control] Given a stored document with a valid acp record, no instructionsDelivered field and no turn marker, when resumeAgentSession restores it with instructions 'RULES', the next AgentSession.send('next') sends text block 'RULES\n\nnext'.

[integration] Given a stored document with a valid acp record, instructionsDelivered false and a turn marker, when resumeAgentSession restores it with instructions 'RULES', the next AgentSession.send('next') sends text block 'RULES\n\nnext'.

[integration] In the delivery fixture with a transcript store whose save throws once only for the write carrying instructionsDelivered: true, the first completed text AgentSession.send logs 'Could not save the ACP instruction delivery' at warn through the logger installed with setAgentLogger from @nathapp/nax-agent, ends with status 'completed', and leaves the stored acp.instructionsDelivered false.

[integration] In the delivery fixture with a transcript store whose save throws once only for the write carrying instructionsDelivered: true, after a first completed text AgentSession.send (whose delivery save fails) and a second completed AgentSession.send, the stored acp.instructionsDelivered is true.
[integration; control] When createAgentSession opens a session with no instructions, the stored document's acp record has no instructionsDelivered field.

[integration] When createAgentSession opens a session with instructions '' and inMemoryAgent answers its first text AgentSession.send with message content, the stored acp record still has no instructionsDelivered field.

[integration; failure handling] Given a stored document with a valid acp identity record, a non-boolean instructionsDelivered value and a turn marker, when resumeAgentSession restores it with instructions 'RULES', the next AgentSession.send('next') reaches inMemoryAgent with text block 'next'.

[integration; failure handling] Given a stored document with a valid acp identity record, a non-boolean instructionsDelivered value and no turn marker, when resumeAgentSession restores it with instructions 'RULES', the next AgentSession.send('next') reaches inMemoryAgent with text block 'RULES\n\nnext'.

routing.reasoning: Four existing source files gain an optional type field, boolean restore extraction, conditional initial metadata and a saveBaseline-style merge helper; these are standard bounded changes, while session resume and persisted instruction state require the three-session-tdd security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: `TranscriptAcpRecord` gains the optional `readonly instructionsDelivered?: boolean` field with a doc comment; this is a type-only change in the nax-agent package that the ACP backend's writes need, with no runtime change in nax-agent.

analysis:
Repository exploration: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host, so findings come from direct source reads and text searches. This is a targeted enhancement of the existing Bun-workspace TypeScript ESM implementation, not a new architecture. Implement exactly US-001, US-002 and US-003 independently, with no dependencies. All retain the binding workdir packages/nax-agent-acp; US-003 additionally has an explicitly authorized type-only edit in packages/nax-agent. No new production dependency, protocol method, transcript migration, or runtime change to nax-agent is required.

US-001 implementation and callers: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/registry.ts:108 creates the per-instance registry. Its setMode and setConfigOption currently read entry metadata and compute their targets before awaiting applySettings (registry.ts:396-406). applySettings delegates a changed target to switchTo and sends mode/config announcements (registry.ts:299-313). switchTo checks running, then awaits credentials for a model change before entering the server switch (registry.ts:245-254). This is the stale-mode window. It already re-reads the current entry after switching to preserve a prompt's title, timestamp and cost (registry.ts:268-278); retain that behavior rather than serializing prompts. ServerSession.switchTo synchronously marks running and clears it in finally (packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/server-session.ts:326-338), while prompt protects bookkeeping under running (server-session.ts:300-325). Add a private per-session settings-tail map and helper within createSessionRegistry; the entire mutation including lookup, derivation, switch, persistence, announcements and returned config options belongs inside the queued work. The idle path must invoke work synchronously, not through Promise.resolve().then(work), because the credential lookup currently starts in the caller's tick. Keep each caller's own rejecting result separate from the muted tail; clean up only when the settling tail is still the stored tail. This avoids poisoned queues, unhandled rejections and an older completion deleting a newer registration. The intended compatibility change is that overlapping settings calls wait instead of receiving turnInProgress from an overlapping switch. The protocol routes already delegate to these methods (packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/connection.ts:71-75); server main constructs the registry (src/server/main.ts:131). No caller API changes are needed.

US-001 resume/delete race: openEntry awaits credentials and acquires the storage lock before its existing cleanup try (registry.ts:189-198), then starts MCP and opens the facade session. Its catch already closes any opened session/MCP and releases the lock (registry.ts:230-236). Add the requireStored existence check inside that try immediately after lock acquisition, before startMcp. unknownSession is the existing SDK resource-not-found mapping (packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/errors.ts:16-18); do not invent another error code. create calls openEntry without requireStored (registry.ts:355), because new metadata does not exist yet. delete closes an open entry or checks hasMeta, takes a lock, deletes transcript and metadata and releases it (registry.ts:383-395); leave it unchanged. createReopen already serializes concurrent load/resume opens using a separate inFlight map (packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/registry-open.ts:50,110-133); the settings queue does not replace this map. ReopenDeps.openEntry needs the optional fourth argument (registry-open.ts:29-33); openStored reads metadata before awaits (registry-open.ts:96-107), so pass requireStored through openAndReplay (registry-open.ts:70-73). Only existence is re-read: preserve the originally selected metadata and existing replay behavior. Tests should use setupRegistry's failOpens, ensureCredentials, opened requests and counted releases (packages/nax-agent-acp/test/helpers/registry-setup.ts:35-55,58-136). The held-credentials and priced-turn patterns already exist in test/unit/server/registry-races.test.ts:16-74; its overlapping resume/load controls at :126-191 protect the separate reopen queue. Sequential mode/config coverage is in test/unit/server/registry-mode.test.ts:57-64,107-137; existing registry switch/close/credentials suites also remain regression anchors. The new registry-settings-queue.test.ts must deterministically signal entry into the held lookup before deleting, release gates in cleanup, and assert precisely three lock releases for close/delete/refused resume.

US-002 implementation and impact: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/turn.ts:106-120 currently constructs state.link.prompt before calling race. race sees an already-aborted signal, but cannot undo the already-dispatched request (src/client/race.ts:18-33). The facade emits turn_start then awaits markTurn(running) before adapter dispatch (packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-turn.ts:198-217); sendTurn also awaits liveFor (packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/backend.ts:353-355). These awaits provide the cancellation window. Add only the pre-dispatch guard in promptOnce, throwing abortReason(signal) with attachTurnSpend(reason, unansweredSpend(carried)); the initial carried usage is absent, so NO_RESPONSE_SPEND yields zero input/output tokens and zero cost (turn.ts:58-72). Do not call cancelTurn when no request exists. The existing post-dispatch cancel path sends a notification and allows the bounded grace before kill/disconnect (turn.ts:163-175); denial continuation already checks !signal.aborted without another await before dispatch (turn.ts:86-95). The facade maps an aborted signal to cancelled and reads attached spend (agent-session-turn.ts:137-158), so no facade code modification is required. New turn-cancel-before-dispatch.test.ts should drive createAgentSession/AgentSession.send rather than just an internal function, wrap the memory store's running marker with a held promise, cancel on turn_start and release it, then verify wire requests and terminal event usage. The existing facade image helpers demonstrate public forwarding (test/unit/client/backend-images.test.ts:37-56). inMemoryAgent records requests and notifications across launches through callsTo (test/helpers/in-memory-launch.ts:13-20,65-73), using the sanctioned _acpBackendDeps.launch seam. Existing cancellation/grace controls are in test/unit/client/backend.test.ts:254-336 and backend-process.test.ts:144-152.

US-003 persistence and compatibility: TranscriptAcpRecord currently holds agent identity, cwd and optional cumulative cost (packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-types.ts:17-28). It is already exported publicly (packages/nax-agent/src/index.ts:202; native/index.ts:60) and used through TranscriptDoc by facade/session/store code. Add only the documented optional readonly boolean; ACP imports it through @nathapp/nax-agent, never internal/deep imports. The API snapshot currently records type names (packages/nax-agent/api/nax-agent.api.txt:356,824); inspect the repository API check if needed, but do not add a new export or assume an export-name change is required. initialDoc constructs the acp record in packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts:394-408 and must add false only for non-empty instructions. Restored opens deliberately do not rewrite the document (open.ts:235-237). Restore/storedSessionOf validate persisted identity, agent and canonical cwd before launch and normalize cost (src/client/resume.ts:28-34,86-114); extract instructionsDelivered only if typeof is boolean without weakening those existing checks or rejecting legacy/malformed optional values. openBackend currently derives instructionsSent solely from the existence of a turn marker (src/client/backend.ts:251-271); explicit false must override even an ended/running marker, explicit true must win, and absent/non-boolean values retain legacy marker behavior. Initialize deliverySaved to the resulting instructionsSent value. sendTurn rejects unsupported images before constructing a collector (backend.ts:353-358), then prefixes instructions and uses onReceipt to update only in-memory instructionsSent (backend.ts:359-367). Preserve the receipt definition: the collector's RECEIPT_KINDS allowlist and one-shot callback distinguish actual prompt work from unsolicited configuration/replay (src/client/events.ts:116-162). Persist true in sendTurn finally after saveBaseline only for non-empty ctx.instructions and unsaved receipt. Like saveBaseline (backend.ts:399-412), saveDelivery must load the latest document, skip missing acp, merge rather than replace metadata, and mark deliverySaved only after successful save. warn already contains throwing host loggers (backend.ts:414-420); use it with the exact instruction-delivery warning. A failed delivery write leaves false persisted and deliverySaved false while instructionsSent remains true, allowing a later completed turn to retry persistence without re-prefixing instructions in the same process. The memory store clones documents and merges markers (packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/memory-transcript-store.ts:15-44), so test wrappers can hold markTurn or fail exactly the true-delivery save without mutating unrelated writes.
